reference.title: Dumbbell Front Squat
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips; Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, lower; breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, a 2 s pause at the bottom, then a barbell front squat. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Rest one end of each dumbbell on the front of the shoulders, palms facing in, elbows forward. Feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Breathe in, brace, sit straight down; knees follow the toes, elbows stay up.
Thighs about parallel or a bit lower, chest tall, heels down.
Drive the floor away and stand tall without letting the elbows drop; breathe out near the top.
Stand tall, reset the brace, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows dropping and the dumbbells sliding off the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing forward and the chest up all the way down.
Push the knees out over the 2nd-3rd toes.
Sit between the heels; widen the stance slightly or shorten the depth.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the upper back under the load
mistakes.fix: Brace before each rep and keep the chest proud.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width, toes out about 15-20 degrees (common coaching; Zawadka 2020 used shoulder width)
About 100-120 degrees with the thighs at parallel or a bit below (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range (Zawadka 2020)
Not specified by the sources for this depth
More upright than a back squat because the load is in front (Gullett 2009; Straub 2024)
Racked on the front of the shoulders, palms in, elbows forward (common coaching; clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, about 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #296612, Dumbbell Front Squat, video (movement reference)
Gullett, Tillman, Gutierrez & Chow 2009, a biomechanical comparison of back and front squats in healthy trained individuals (J Strength Cond Res 23(1):284-292; PubMed 19002072)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: squat to a box or a shallower depth.
Wrist or shoulder discomfort in the rack: hold one dumbbell as a goblet squat instead.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat. With the load in front, the front squat recruited the muscles about as much as the back squat with less knee compressive force (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Knee extensors lower and drive the squat. With the load in front, the front squat recruited the muscles about as much as the back squat with less knee compressive force (Gullett 2009).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor, working hardest out of the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension in the deep squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Co-contract around the knee and assist hip extension (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the shins as the knees travel forward over the toes.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk under a load carried in front of the spine.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up; the front load keeps the trunk more upright than a back squat (Gullett 2009 measured trunk angle in both squats).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up; the front load keeps the trunk more upright than a back squat (Gullett 2009 measured trunk angle in both squats).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders up as a shelf for the dumbbells (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders up as a shelf for the dumbbells (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Keeps the elbows forward so the dumbbells stay on the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Keeps the elbows forward so the dumbbells stay on the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the elbows bent with the dumbbells on the shoulders (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent with the dumbbells on the shoulders (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Stand tall, dumbbells on the shoulders
